question.text: Two satellites <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> move round the earth in the same orbit. The mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is twice the mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math>. The quantity which is same for the two satellites will be

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the speed of a satellite while revolving around the Earth is given by

v=GMeR   ...1

where, v is the speed, G is the Gravitational constant, Me is the mass of the Earth, R is the radius of the orbit.

As can be seen from the equation, speed is independent of mass of satellite.

Hence, the speed of the satellites will be the same.
